batch: 5 (chs 36-39, the Hezekiah narrative - NARRATIVE SCENES, genre shift like Jonah)

units.characteristics: the assault on trust; psychological warfare against the interior's confidence
units.gist: the Rabshakeh's speech - 'ON WHAT DO YOU REST THIS TRUST of yours? In whom do you now trust?'; 'do not let Hezekiah make you TRUST IN THE LORD'; 'has any of the gods delivered his land?' - the enemy's strategy is to undermine faith itself, corrode confidence in God; the people's disciplined silence ('do not answer him')

units.characteristics: the threat spread before the LORD; trust brought to God in prayer
units.gist: GEM - Hezekiah tears his clothes, goes to the house of the LORD; 'children come to birth and there is no strength to bring them forth' (the interior at the end of itself); he 'SPREAD IT [the letter] BEFORE THE LORD' and prayed 'you alone are God... SAVE US, that all the kingdoms may know that you alone are the LORD'; against Sennacherib's boast 'BY MY MANY CHARIOTS I have gone up'; the deliverance

units.characteristics: the interior facing death; suffering reframed as welfare; the gratitude of the living
units.gist: GEM - mortally ill, Hezekiah 'turned his FACE TO THE WALL and prayed', 'wept bitterly'; God adds 15 years; his writing - 'in the middle of my days I must depart... my eyes are weary with looking upward'; 'IT WAS FOR MY WELFARE that I had great bitterness; but in love you have delivered my life from the pit, for you have CAST ALL MY SINS BEHIND YOUR BACK'; 'the LIVING, THE LIVING, he thanks you'

units.characteristics: pride after deliverance; complacency that cares only for its own days
units.gist: GEM (cautionary) - the Babylonian envoys; Hezekiah 'welcomed them GLADLY and SHOWED THEM his treasure house... all that was in his storehouses' (self-display after being healed); the prophecy of exile; 'the word of the LORD is good', for he thought 'THERE WILL BE PEACE AND SECURITY IN MY DAYS' - the subtle pride and self-content in the aftermath of grace
